id: title:Gilbert09:keep redshift server cursor on single node clusters

review.posthog_relevance: Redshift warehouse ingestion connector: P1.F1.H1 adds a Redshift-specific constant and error detection; P1.F1.H2 adds a configurable fetch size parameter; P1.F1.H3 implements a retry strategy with reduced fetch size. This collectively establishes a bounded, retry-capable ingestion path for Redshift, preserving server-side cursors and avoiding OOM failures on single-node clusters.
review.reason: Adds Redshift-specific error detection, a configurable fetch size parameter, and an automatic retry strategy with reduced fetch size. This establishes a bounded, retry-capable ingestion path for Redshift, preserving server-side cursors and avoiding OOM failures on single-node clusters.
review.uncertainty: The tier is assigned based on the presence of a substantive, bounded capability and its implementation. The tier does not account for unverified outcomes, such as actual ingestion success or incident avoidance, which are not demonstrated by the code alone.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No missing context or truncation. No score assigned yet.

observations.behavior: Adds a Redshift-specific constant and a helper to detect the exact error message, and a retry strategy.
observations.posthog_connection: Redshift warehouse ingestion: the connector now detects the 1000-row fetch limit on single-node clusters and will retry with a smaller fetch size instead of immediately falling back to a client-side read, preserving the server-side cursor and avoiding OOM. This could prevent ingestion failures and worker crashes when syncing large tables to Redshift.

observations.behavior: Adds a helper to distinguish the Redshift fetch-size error and a new parameter to control per-fetch page size.
observations.posthog_connection: Redshift warehouse ingestion: the connector now accepts a per-fetch page size, allowing it to stay under the 1000-row limit while still accumulating rows into larger Arrow batches. This preserves the server-side cursor and avoids the 1000-row fetch rejection, keeping ingestion reliable and memory-bounded.

observations.behavior: Adds a retry loop that first tries the requested chunk size, then retries at the Redshift single-node fetch limit if the first attempt fails with the fetch-size error.
observations.posthog_connection: Redshift warehouse ingestion: the connector now automatically retries the query with a smaller fetch size when the first attempt fails with the Redshift-specific fetch-size error, rather than immediately falling back to a client-side read. This preserves the server-side cursor and avoids OOM and ingestion failures on single-node Redshift clusters.
